title: What is the smallest multiple of nine with no odd digits?
description: The digit sum rule for nine is used to find the smallest multiple of nine whose digits are all even. The video shows that the digit sum must be eighteen or more, so the number needs three digits.
teaching_notes: One idea: even digits always add to an even number, so the digit sum of such a multiple of nine is eighteen or more. Watch for students who test one multiple of nine after another and never explain why the number cannot have fewer digits.

source: Figure it Out (multiples of nine, question 2)
video_script.why: The student knows that a number and its digit sum are divisible by nine together and now uses the digit sum to build a number.
video_script.substitution: Find the smallest possible digit sum for even digits, then find the fewest digits that can give it and make the number as small as possible.
video_script.anchor: boxes for the digits of a number, with a strip of even multiples of nine beside them
video_script.payoff_line: The smallest such number is two hundred eighty eight
maths_rules: a number is divisible by 9 exactly when its digit sum is divisible by 9
even digits always add to an even number, so the digit sum is an even multiple of 9: 18 or more
two even digits add to at most 8 + 8 = 16, less than 18, so the number needs three digits
the hundreds digit cannot be 0 and 1 is odd, so the smallest hundreds digit is 2
the other two digits add to 18 - 2 = 16, and only 8 and 8 do
video_script.design: Boxes for the digits and a strip of even multiples of nine. The strip shows that eighteen is the smallest possible digit sum, and the boxes show that two digits cannot reach it.
